name: Constitutional Monarchism
summary: Constitutional monarchism holds that a hereditary monarch, bound by a constitution and acting on the advice of elected ministers, is a good head of state. Supporters argue the Crown stands above party as a symbol of national unity, supplies continuity and ceremony, and acts as a check on elected politicians. It takes no fixed line on economics or social policy.
scope: The mainstream modern strand in parliamentary monarchies (UK, Commonwealth realms, Western European monarchies), drawing on Walter Bagehot's The English Constitution, Vernon Bogdanor's account of the monarch who reigns but does not rule, and the programme of the Monarchist League of Canada. It excludes absolutists and sacral monarchs (for example Thailand), and legitimist or restorationist movements. Because the ideology is a theory of the head of state, many statements on economics and social issues are answered 0 with low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The monarchist case concerns the head of state, not health policy; adherents in Britain, Scandinavia and elsewhere span left and right on this.

public-ownership.rationale: Nothing in constitutional monarchism bears on ownership of industry; adherents differ by party.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation levels are left to elected governments; monarchists as such are split.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not a monarchist concern; adherents differ with their wider party politics.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No monarchist position on corporate regulation; adherents split by party.

cut-welfare.rationale: Adherents include both welfare-state conservatives and social liberals; no doctrinal answer.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: No doctrinal position; constitutional monarchies differ (lese-majeste laws exist in some), and adherents split.

strong-leader.rationale: The model is a monarch who reigns but does not rule, with power exercised by parliament and ministers, so a leader bypassing gridlock cuts against it.

state-harmful.rationale: Monarchists defend the state and its institutions; the Crown is itself a state institution that supporters credit with providing continuity and checks.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun control is not tied to the monarchist case; views vary by country and party.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: A morals-policy issue on which monarchists are split, with no doctrinal answer.

decide-locally.rationale: Monarchism is compatible with both unitary and federal states (Canada, Belgium, UK); supporters stress the Crown as a national unifier but not centralisation.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is not part of the monarchist case; adherents differ.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Monarchists in constitutional monarchies back both sides; several monarchies legalised it under royal assent without monarchist opposition as such.

abortion-legal.rationale: A conscience issue on which adherents are split; not part of the doctrine.

more-religion-public.rationale: Monarchist groups value the Crown's Christian ceremonial but accept non-religious participation, so the position is mixed.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: No doctrinal position; adherents divide along party lines.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Outside the doctrine; adherents are split.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Monarchist leagues present ceremony, heritage and tradition as cohesive national forces worth keeping.

gradual-change.rationale: Supporters defend inherited institutions and argue republicans have shown no clear advantage in changing them, so cautious evolution is their stock approach.

free-trade.rationale: Trade policy is not part of the doctrine; adherents differ.

nation-first.rationale: The Crown is presented as a national symbol, but constitutional monarchists include internationalists, so there is no clear position.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign policy is left to ministers under the convention that the monarch acts on advice; no doctrinal answer.

limit-growth.rationale: No relation to monarchist doctrine; adherents differ.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not a monarchist issue; views follow party affiliation.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy is outside the doctrine; adherents split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Monarchists stress continuity and gradual, lawful change, and the whole model is to keep constitutional order stable against upheaval.

experts-over-public.rationale: Bagehot's cabinet government rests on elected Commons and public deference rather than rule by experts, though he doubts mass wisdom; adherents lean toward elected parliaments.

land-value-tax.rationale: No relation to the monarchist case.

basic-income.rationale: Welfare design is left to elected governments; adherents split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing money and wages is a revolutionary programme alien to a movement defending inherited institutions and gradual change.

one-party-rule.rationale: Constitutional monarchy is described as a safeguard against dictatorship, and monarchs are held to stand above party; a ruling single party is the opposite.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The defining claim: Wikipedia and monarchist groups present a hereditary monarch as a legitimate, unifying head of state under a constitution.

democracy-best.rationale: Constitutional monarchists generally pair the Crown with parliamentary democracy, though the Crown is also valued as a check on elected politicians, so the endorsement is qualified.

direct-votes.rationale: Bagehot's cabinet government works through the elected Commons, not direct popular lawmaking, and Hobbes-style arguments distrust passion-driven assemblies; representative parliament is the norm.

workers-councils.rationale: Power rests with parliament and the Crown under a constitution; councils replacing parliaments are a revolutionary alternative.

right-to-secede.rationale: Monarchists point to the Crown as a symbol uniting multinational states such as Belgium and the UK, which makes secession unwelcome.

natural-rulers.rationale: C.S. Lewis and Kuehnelt-Leddihn defend natural hierarchy, but constitutional monarchists generally accept elected rule, so adherents are split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not a stated tenet; modern constitutional monarchists largely view war as a duty rather than an ennobling process.

separate-church-state.rationale: Monarchist groups value the Crown's Christian coronation rites, and several monarchies are linked to an established church, so strict separation is not the adherent norm.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Constitutional monarchy is rule under constitutional law with parliament making law; religion is ceremonial, not the source of law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Hoppe-style monarchists exist, but the mainstream constitutional view treats courts and defence as state functions under the Crown.

military-superiority.rationale: Defence posture is for ministers; not a monarchist tenet.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Monarchists cite the Crown uniting multinational and multi-ethnic states, so a single-ethnicity nation is not required.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Monarchism stresses national unity and continuity; class conflict as history's engine is a rival, Marxist framework.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hierarchy is accepted as natural by Lewis and Kuehnelt-Leddihn, who say equality is pursued at liberty's expense.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: No doctrinal position; in Commonwealth realms the Crown holds treaty relationships, but adherents differ on remedies.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Conservative strands value duty, while constitutional monarchism claims to protect liberty; adherents split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The value of nature is an environmental-ethics question that the sources on monarchy never raise.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The movement prizes continuity and respect for existing institutions over disruption.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption policy is a modern technical question with no link to the monarchist case.

restore-past-order.rationale: Restorationist monarchists put the old order first while most constitutional monarchists accept modern democracy, so adherents are split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Bagehot is empirical, but supporters defend the Crown on principle; split.

direct-action.rationale: Constitutional monarchists work through parliament and elections; extra-parliamentary direct action is not their method.

means-match-ends.rationale: Prefigurative method is a radical-left idea; monarchists simply favour lawful, constitutional means without framing it this way.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Radically opposed to the preservation of inherited civil institutions that the doctrine defends.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: An anti-industrial revolutionary proposal at odds with an order that includes a constitutional ruling hierarchy.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist maxim; adherents reject the radical programme though not through explicit statements in the sources.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Monarchists present constitutional monarchy as a safeguard against dictatorship of any kind.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Rejecting a Marxist thesis; monarchists in practice endorse existing orders.

taxation-theft.rationale: Constitutional monarchism affirms parliament's budgetary authority and the state; only libertarian monarchists like Hoppe dissent.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Voting through parliament is the mainstream monarchist check on government; exit-first is a libertarian view.

media-academia-power.rationale: Claims about media and universities are a culture-war theme not found in the monarchist sources.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not a monarchist doctrine; mainstream adherents reject racial claims, though unstated.

organic-representation.rationale: Constitutional monarchists generally accept party-based parliaments, which Bagehot analyses; corporate representation is a minority tradition.

total-state.rationale: Monarchy is promoted as a check on power and a safeguard of liberty; a total state is the opposite.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rebirth rhetoric conflicts with the continuity emphasis of monarchists.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Modern constitutional monarchy is rule under constitution and convention, not lord-and-vassal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is incompatible with constitutional monarchy under law.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: An epistemological thesis from critical theory that monarchist sources do not engage.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: A Zionist question with no connection to the case for constitutional monarchy.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are a nationality-law question not raised in the monarchy sources.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Governance of firms is outside the monarchist case; adherents differ by party.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education funding is ordinary party politics, not a monarchist tenet.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is left to elected governments under the convention that the monarch acts on advice.

economic-freedom.rationale: Hoppe says monarchy better protects liberty, but the doctrine is not specifically about economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: The monarch as a moral example is part of ceremonial tradition, but constitutional monarchy relies on law and ministers; split.

national-self-determination.rationale: Monarchists value national Crowns but also hold multinational states together; no single stance.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Monarchist tradition values ceremony, religion and sentiment; Bagehot treats mystery as a source of the monarchy's strength.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility rules are ordinary party politics, not a monarchist tenet.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work requirements for benefits are a policy matter on which monarchists split by party.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Monarchist leagues stress heritage and tradition as cohesive forces to preserve.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Modern constitutional monarchies have moved to equal succession, and mainstream adherents accept equal rights; some traditionalists differ.

ban-interest.rationale: Not a monarchist tenet; established monarchies have financial markets.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Constitutional monarchists defend equal-rights constitutional democracies; segregation is repudiated.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Monarchists present the Crown as above class and party, representing the whole nation, which denies this thesis.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy-supply policy has no link to the monarchist case.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy thesis not part of mainstream constitutional monarchism, which presents the Crown as a unifier.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are open; several monarchies use PR and others not.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale infers the answer from the subject being or backing the establishment, not from a stated view of how politicians behave.

reviewHistory.rationale: Hobbes-derived and Feeney arguments portray the monarch as insulated from corruption in contrast to elected leaders, but monarchists generally accept elected politicians as legitimate.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is not part of the doctrine, and constitutional monarchists defend equal rights.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Transitional-justice questions are not raised in the monarchy sources.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The minimal state is a libertarian idea; some monarchist writers like Hoppe share it but the mainstream does not.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Dynastic marriages historically crossed national lines, and mainstream adherents reject such discouragement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality before the law is accepted in constitutional monarchies, but monarchists defend natural hierarchy (Lewis), so the answer is split.

socialism-one-country.rationale: An internal Marxist debate unconnected to monarchism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: A postcolonial characterisation of settler states; Commonwealth realms with a Crown are split on it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Canadian league grounds the Crown in the consent of a free people, though other monarchist writers also stress tradition and succession.

population-transfer.rationale: Mainstream constitutional monarchists reject forced removal of minorities as against constitutional law.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A libertarian non-aggression axiom; monarchist sources do not endorse it, and monarchies maintain armies and police.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: A social-Darwinist thesis not found in monarchist sources, which emphasise unity and continuity.

separated-powers.rationale: The monarchy is presented as a check and balance against elected politicians, and Montesquieu's separation of powers is cited in the article.

vanguard-party.rationale: Rule by a vanguard party is the opposite of a Crown above party.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: British housing policy is ordinary party politics, with no monarchist stance.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Industrial relations law is party politics; no monarchist tenet.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Lottery rule is foreign to the monarchist model, which has hereditary head of state and elected parliament.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Constitutional monarchy is promoted as safeguard against dictatorship; Hegel sees the monarch giving continuity in emergencies but under constitutional limits.

party-controls-media.rationale: Monarchists claim the institution protects liberty, and the Crown stands outside party; control of media by a ruling party conflicts.

party-commands-army.rationale: In constitutional monarchies the Crown is formal commander-in-chief above party, so party command is opposed.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Attachment to a national Crown inclines adherents against supranational pooling, though many monarchies belong to the EU; split.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Formally the monarch is commander-in-chief and appoints ministers, but by convention acts on advice, so mainstream adherents reject real personal command and choice.

clerical-rule.rationale: Constitutional monarchy is rule under constitutional law and parliament, not clergy; the Thai case shows only a monarch defending religion.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A loyal, national, Crown-centred outlook rules out working for one's own government's defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Constitutional monarchists claim to protect liberty; censorship for virtue is not a tenet.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Hobbes-style and Feeney arguments set the non-partisan monarch against elected leaders who accumulate power; limits on elected office fit.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is a direct-democracy device foreign to Bagehot-style parliamentary government.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is a ministerial question not tied to the Crown.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: A drastic property intervention far from the doctrine.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is a case-specific matter, not a monarchist tenet.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Some traditionalists romanticise the countryside, but the doctrine does not.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: A populist claim about graduates; monarchist sources do not make it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Censorship of pornography is a moral-policy question with no monarchist doctrine.

minority-language-support.rationale: Monarchs in Belgium and Canada represent multilingual states, but there is no doctrinal view.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's argument for individuality is not a monarchist theme, which prizes custom and ceremony.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt relief is a development-policy question unconnected to the monarchist case.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A revolutionary economic doctrine foreign to monarchism.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Monarchists defend the existing constitution as a continuity of tradition; rewriting by assembly is a republican method.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Monarchists present the institution as liberty-protecting.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear posture is a defence-policy matter for ministers.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Opposing an elected head of state is the central monarchist claim: Bogdanor and the Canadian league argue a hereditary monarch stands above party while elected presidents are partisan.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions are a case-specific foreign-policy matter.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: An internal left debate about the USSR, with no monarchist stake.

collective-defense.rationale: Many constitutional monarchies are NATO allies, but the doctrine is silent.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The legal status of annexed territory is a case-specific question; no monarchist doctrine applies.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Where monarchs head a national church, state-church relations are a matter of national history, and adherents split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The defining argument: Bogdanor and the Canadian league describe the monarch as a non-partisan symbol of national unity above parties.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Monarchists value the Crown uniting states, but the use of force is a separate question.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Constitutional monarchists defend a symbolic hereditary head under law; sacral kingship (Thai, Japanese) is a different tradition, and modern Western adherents do not claim divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design is left to elected governments; no monarchist position.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Constitutional monarchy is by definition a monarchy bound by a constitution, with the monarch bound by convention to act on ministers' advice.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Constitutional monarchy is the classic mixed constitution of Crown, lords and commons; Bagehot analyses these elements together.

leader-cult.rationale: Monarchists defend ceremonial royal tradition but the cult of a political leader contrasts with a leader who is non-partisan symbol; moderate disagreement.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis outside the doctrine.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Constitutional monarchy is a liberal-democratic form; punishing apostasy is not accepted.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not accepted by liberal constitutional monarchists.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is a policy question; monarchies including Denmark and Netherlands differ, so no common position.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural autonomy is an Austro-Marxist idea; monarchist sources only note that the Crown unifies multinational states.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Monarchists stress tradition and symbol; Bagehot's emphasis on ceremony and sentiment contradicts this.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is ordinary economic policy with no monarchist angle.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank rescue policy is left to governments; monarchists are split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Constitutional monarchists value checks on elected majorities, and Feeney credits monarchies with checking populism.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for public bodies are party politics, with no monarchist doctrine.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-agreement content is a policy question with no monarchist stake.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Revolution is the opposite of continuity.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Constitutional monarchists defend the hereditary Crown (s1), but the statement concerns hereditary titles and privileges generally, and many accept reforms such as removing hereditary peers from the House of Lords in 1999.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Imperial rule is historically monarchist but modern constitutional monarchists do not endorse it.

patriotic-education.rationale: Heritage and loyalty to the Crown are valued by monarchist leagues, but schooling is not specifically addressed.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is a party-political issue, not a monarchist tenet.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is a heterodox economics view with no connection to monarchism.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Commonwealth supporters value Crown links to former realms, but the doctrine does not require influence-seeking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis unconnected to monarchism.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Monarchy is promoted as a check, but constitutional monarchies such as the UK historically rely on parliamentary supremacy, so adherents are split.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Validity of colonial treaties is a case-specific matter; the Crown is a treaty party in some realms but monarchists have no common view.

elective-rulers.rationale: The defining republican alternative to monarchy; Wikipedia identifies succession by heredity with the institution.

minority-veto.rationale: A single dissenter binding no one conflicts with Bagehot-style parliamentary majority government.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Constitutional monarchy rests on the monarch being bound by constitution; impeachment is among Bagehot's checks against gross abuse, and Hegel-type limits apply.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Under constitutional monarchy, power is exercised by Parliament and government on the monarch's behalf, with the monarch bound by convention to follow ministerial advice.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Defenders of hierarchy such as C.S. Lewis argue that rank carries duties, and royal patronage of charity reflects it, though the sources do not set it out as a tenet.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian hegemony thesis not engaged by monarchist sources; Bagehot's deference and ceremony resemble it but he does not frame it so.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency-theory claim unconnected to monarchism.

native-born-offices.rationale: Succession rules have historically emphasised national lineage, but the doctrine does not address public offices generally.

party-own-road.rationale: An internal communist-movement question outside monarchism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not a monarchist view; the Crown stands above group claims.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Monarchists present constitutional monarchy as a safeguard against all dictatorship, so condemning both is natural, though unstated.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A US history dispute unconnected to monarchism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Heritage and tradition are central to monarchist leagues; monuments are not specifically addressed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Monarchists defend inherited local institutions, but constitutional monarchists do not deny democratic institutions elsewhere.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Constitutional monarchy keeps the military under civilian ministerial advice, with the monarch as a check, rather than a political guardian army.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Investment screening is an economic-policy question unrelated to the Crown.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is a social-policy matter on which monarchists split.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding delegates with instant recall contradicts Bagehot's model of ministers answerable to Commons and a Crown above them.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is party economic policy, not a monarchist tenet.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliament's control of supply is the historic heart of constitutional monarchy: the monarch acts through ministers answerable to the Commons.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: A cultural critique on which conservatives and liberals both divide.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert foreign policy is for ministers; no monarchist doctrine applies.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Regulation of foreign funding is a sovereignty-policy matter without monarchist doctrine.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Family-incentive policy is party politics with no monarchist stance.

democratic-peace.rationale: Monarchist sources praise constitutional monarchy as a form of democracy but do not discuss international relations theory.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Monarchists rest on law, constitution and loyalty to the Crown; denying a general duty to obey conflicts.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is a labour-movement question without monarchist stake.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy claims against minorities are alien to a doctrine presenting the Crown as unifier.

religious-nation.rationale: Monarchist leagues note non-religious citizens can take part in the Crown's ceremonies, so national membership is not religiously defined.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not a monarchist doctrine; Belgium, Spain and Canada show monarchies with differing settlements.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Conservative institutionalism upholds private property; the statement presupposes common ownership of production, so only weak agreement.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public-service delivery models are party policy, not monarchist doctrine.

religion-illusion.rationale: Bagehot treats religion and mystery as vital to the monarchy's hold on the public, and the monarchist league defends Christian ceremony, so religion-as-illusion is rejected.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of childcare is party politics with no monarchist stance.

treaties-binding.rationale: In Commonwealth realms the Crown is party to treaties, but adherents have no stated view.

majority-settlement.rationale: Monarchists present the Crown as unifying minorities; engineered settlement is contrary.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Mainstream constitutional monarchists, including royal-family figures, accept the historical record; not part of the doctrine.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Constitutional monarchy is a safeguard against dictatorship, and the loyal opposition is part of the system Bagehot describes.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine of war with no connection to constitutional monarchism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Bagehot's model is representative cabinet government; direct decisions by ordinary people are not its idea.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A critical-theory claim not engaged by monarchist sources.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Transgender legal recognition is a social-policy dispute on which adherents split.

assisted-dying.rationale: A conscience question with no monarchist doctrine.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept that monarchist sources do not engage.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Local franchise for foreigners is a policy question with no monarchist stance.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property reform is not a monarchist theme.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Basing policy is a ministerial matter with no Crown stake.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Basing policy is a ministerial matter with no Crown stake.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Official recognition of past atrocities is a diplomatic matter with no monarchist doctrine.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Continuity and long history are central to the Canadian league's case for the Crown, though a claim of ancient national origins is not specifically stated.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Cultural Zionism is unconnected to constitutional monarchism.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Contrary to the Crown as unifier of all subjects.

independent-unions.rationale: Union independence is a labour question with no monarchist stake.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: An internal socialist definition with no monarchist stake.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public ownership of local services is party economic policy.

second-chamber.rationale: Bagehot discusses the House of Lords as a second chamber of constitutional monarchy, and most constitutional monarchies have one.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not a monarchist doctrine; monarchists value a unified Crown.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Payment privacy is a technical policy question with no monarchist stance.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online identity policy has no connection to the monarchist case.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The league treats Christian rites as meaningful to believers while including non-religious citizens.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Contrary to a Crown representing the whole nation.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Constitutional monarchies conduct foreign policy through ministers; no monarchist doctrine on just-war limits.

communal-electorates.rationale: Not a doctrine; Crown stands above communities.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Conspiracy thinking is not part of the doctrine.

free-public-college.rationale: Tuition policy is party politics with no monarchist stance.

women-distinct-values.rationale: A difference-feminist claim outside the monarchist case.

arms-reduction.rationale: Arms control is a ministerial question not tied to the Crown.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital-flow policy is party economics with no monarchist stance.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Constitutional monarchs command forces by ministerial advice; soldier refusal conflicts with loyalty.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Wage-setting method is industrial-relations policy not tied to monarchism.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax-credit design is party economic policy.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Contrary to continuity and a constitutional state preserved.

sacred-nation.rationale: Ceremony binds the national community, but the league does not use sacral language.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student debt policy is party politics with no monarchist stance.

public-service-media.rationale: Public broadcasting is policy not specific to monarchism, though several monarchies have strong public broadcasters.

farm-price-support.rationale: Agricultural policy is party economics with no monarchist stance.

workers-own-party.rationale: Labour-party formation is a socialist debate unconnected to monarchism.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Sentencing policy is not part of the monarchist case; the royal prerogative of mercy exists but is not argued over.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Constitutional monarchy is government bound by a constitution and law, so state killing without trial conflicts with its core principle.

self-ownership.rationale: The ideology takes no fixed line on social or economic philosophy, so adherents are split on self-ownership.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The ideology takes no fixed line on economics or social policy; adherents differ.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The ideology takes no fixed line on economics; adherents differ on business privileges.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Supporters of the Crown include established churches and secular monarchies, and the ideology takes no fixed line on this; adherents are split.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The ideology requires a monarch bound by a constitution and elected ministers, and a Crown standing above party contradicts one-party rule.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Adherents include both welfare-state conservatives and social liberals; no doctrinal answer. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: The head of state should reign but not rule, acting on the advice of the elected government.
missingStatements.rationale: Bogdanor's formula, quoted in the Wikipedia article, is that a constitutional monarch reigns but does not rule, bound by convention to act on ministerial advice.

missingStatements.text: A head of state who is not elected should keep reserve powers to act in a constitutional crisis.
missingStatements.rationale: Commonwealth realms vest reserve powers in the monarch and governors-general for extreme emergencies, and supporters after the 1975 Australian crisis saw them as a check on elected politicians.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow constitutional detail; monarchy-legitimate and nonpartisan-head-of-state cover the position.

notes: Strands differ on how much real power the monarch should keep: Bagehot allows influence through consultation and warning, while strict ceremonialists want none. Libertarian monarchists (Hoppe) and sacral monarchies (Thailand, Japan) would answer several statements differently. Many answers are 0 low because the ideology concerns the head of state, not economic or social policy.
